notes: Ran an iceless R&D four times a turn, so most runs saw the same top card again. It never installed a card, spent 6 credits removing 3 of 4 tags and sat at 0 credits while the Corp scored three agendas out of one remote protected only by Enigma.

Recovered well from an early Account Siphon by fast-advancing Breaking News out of new remotes and scoring behind Resistor. R&D stayed open for a long time and it lingered at 1 credit, but the plan held together.

Spent three whole turns clicking for credits up to 24 while discarding cards, never set up a hand big enough to steal Obokata, and turned down a steal of Send a Message. It then ran into a known Loki/Anansi server with 5 cards and got flatlined.

Agendas were protected sensibly and the Archer rez was a good play. But it clicked for credits for many turns while sitting on 13-29 credits, drew into discards and took 20 turns to close against a passive Runner.

Twice used Turntable to swap a freshly stolen higher-value agenda for a lower one, which handed the Corp points. It also bled money paying to remove tags after every IP Block run, wasted a click and credits installing a second unique Turning Wheel, and used Stimhacks for trivial accesses.

Banked 20-27 credits by clicking for money but never rezzed the outer remote ice, and it played Economic Warfare for no effect. It then put Project Atlas and two GFIs one after another into a remote the Runner had already shown it could walk into.

Kept up steady pressure on R&D with Yog.0 and won, but it twice spent Inside Job to bypass an Enigma that Yog breaks for free. It also left the scoring remote alone and clicked for credits while rich.

Ran an iceless R&D four times on turn one, then installed nothing all game and clicked for credits up to 31. Meanwhile the Corp advanced and scored four agendas over several turns in remotes the Runner never ran.
Built a deep remote and scored from it steadily. It played Biotic Labor only to click for credits, and it let agendas pile up in a weakly iced Archives, where the Runner stole 4 points.
Built solid IPO economy, iced up the remote and scored two SDS Drone Deployments and SSL Endorsement in a row. Its few slow turns clicking for credits could have gone into advancing.
Scored efficiently out of two iced remotes while IP Block kept the Runner's AI out. Its only oddities were a few minor passive turns and end-of-turn discards.

Lowered its own hand size with repeated Stimhacks, then kept drawing three cards and discarding them. It installed a second unique Knobkierie that was trashed at once, and at 6 points it stole SSL Endorsement with 1 card in grip and 3 credits against a Corp already seen playing Punitive Counterstrike, and was flatlined.

Never installed a single agenda in 30 turns and spent most clicks gaining credits up to 29 and discarding. It kept the agendas in an HQ guarded by one or two ice, and the Runner stole all of them there.

Early multi-access runs were fine, but from mid-game it clicked for credits up to 23 every turn. It never once ran the remote where the Corp scored Offworld Office, Project Atlas and Hostile Takeover.

Good Temujin R&D economy, made good use of Film Critic, and finished by building a full rig to break into the remote. Minor oddities were a duplicate Temujin Contract that got trashed and a fairly slow middle game.

Spent a whole turn on Consulting Visit into Audacity, which threw away its HQ (including Hostile Takeover, stolen from Archives) for nothing. It played Dedication Ceremony on Runner cards and installed a second Offworld Office into a remote the Runner had just broken.

Kept a single R&D access each turn and won, but it was slow and low-impact. It spent a lot of clicks and credits removing Turnpike tags and never pushed multi-access against a Corp that scored nothing.
Spent about seven turns clicking for credits up to 34 while discarding cards, and lost Obokata from an HQ guarded only by Konjin. It eventually scored three agendas from an iced remote.

Left Breaking News naked in a remote overnight and it was stolen, and it clicked for credits early. The rest was a sensible mix of fast-advanced Breaking News and scoring from an iced remote with AstroScript.

Repeatedly ran an iceless R&D four times a turn seeing the same card while the Corp advanced GFI in a remote. After bouncing off Border Control once, it clicked for credits for eight turns up to 51 and never ran again while the Corp scored two Project Atlas.
